tasks.spec:
You are an Elixir/OTP engineer fixing two small, independent bugs. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the Cornerman repo, an Elixir/OTP port of the Ringer agent-swarm tool. Edit files here directly.

NEVER TOUCH: anything under test/ (the tests are the acceptance check), DIVERGENCES.toml, bin/, mix.exs, mix.lock, .git, and every file under lib/ except the two below. Do not git commit, push or git add. Do not add dependencies.

OWNED PATHS (the only files you may create or edit): lib/cornerman/spawn/run.ex, lib/cornerman/py/json.ex and ./notes.md. Keep each fix inside its own file; they will be committed separately.

BUG 1, lib/cornerman/py/json.ex. `Cornerman.Py.Json` decodes JSON the way Python's json module does (Python 3.12.13). A number literal that overflows a double must become inf (or -inf), as Python's float() does, and one that underflows must become 0.0 (or -0.0). `float/4` tries `:erlang.binary_to_float/1` and on ArgumentError calls `saturate/3`, which returns zero whenever the exponent is negative. That is wrong for a large mantissa with a small negative exponent: `1` followed by 400 zeros then `.5e-10` is about 1e390, so Python gives inf and lint prints `cornerman: error: cannot convert float infinity to integer` for it as max_parallel, but Cornerman says `max_parallel must be positive`. Verified on this OTP 28: `:erlang.binary_to_float/1` raises only on overflow; underflow returns 0.0 or -0.0 (`"1.0e-400"`, `"1.0e-99999999999999999999"`, `"100.0e-400"` all give 0.0) and an all-zero mantissa gives 0.0 at any exponent (`"0.0e999"`). Decide from what the failure actually means. The conformance case is lint/error-float-overflow-negative-exponent (test/conformance/fixtures/lint/). Compare with the oracle: `RINGER_NO_SELF_UPDATE=1 /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3 /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py/ringer.py lint <manifest>` against `bin/cornerman lint <manifest>`.

BUG 2, lib/cornerman/spawn/run.ex. `Cornerman.Spawn.Run` (lib/cornerman/spawn/run.ex) owns one OS command started with erlexec (`:exec.run/2` with the `:link` option, which returns `{:ok, lwp, os_pid}`, where `lwp` is erlexec's per-command Erlang process). The Run process traps exits and treats an `{:EXIT, _, reason}` message with reason `:normal` or `{:exit_status, _}` as "the command's leader has exited". But Run also sends signals to the process group with `System.cmd("kill", ...)`, and each System.cmd opens a port linked to Run; when that port closes, a trapping process receives `{:EXIT, port, :normal}` (verified: `Process.flag(:trap_exit, true); System.cmd("true", [])` delivers `{:EXIT, #Port<...>, :normal}`). So on a timeout or stop, Run takes the kill command's port exit for the leader's exit. Consequences: (1) the caller gets `{:exit, :timeout}` / `{:exit, :stopped}` right after SIGTERM goes out, while a leader that ignores SIGTERM is still running, which breaks the module's contract (the exit event comes once the command has exited); (2) Run then stops right after sending SIGKILL, before erlexec has reaped the leader; erlexec sees Run's link go down, asks its port program to stop the OS pid, and the port program's kill of the group fails, which erlexec logs as `[:exec] unknown msg: {:error, :eperm}` (once per spawn-suite run, from the test at "timeout kills the worker's grandchildren, even ones ignoring SIGTERM").

THE FIX must make Run recognise only the exit of its own erlexec process as the leader's exit, and ignore EXIT messages from anything else it is linked to (the kill ports). Keep every existing behaviour described in the moduledoc of lib/cornerman/spawn.ex and in the comments in run.ex: SIGTERM, grace, SIGKILL of the whole group; exactly one exit event; `:timeout`/`:stopped` reported instead of the status after a kill was requested; the owner-down path; erlexec's kill_group/kill_timeout as the fallback. Keep the change small and in the existing style.

THE TESTS: the conformance case lint/error-float-overflow-negative-exponent (bug 1) and, in test/cornerman/spawn_test.exs, "the exit event waits for a leader that ignores SIGTERM to die" (bug 2) fail today and must pass; everything else must stay green.

SETUP (run once, first, from this directory; the sandbox cannot fetch packages):
  cp -R /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/deps ./deps
  export PATH=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/elixir/1.20.1-otp-28/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/erlang/28.5/bin:$PATH HEX_OFFLINE=1 CORNERMAN_ORACLE=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py CORNERMAN_PYTHON=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3

HOW TO RUN (after the setup, from this directory):
  MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix format
  mix test test/conformance                  # lint parity, bug 1
  mix test test/cornerman/spawn_test.exs     # bug 2; run it several times with --seed N and look for "unknown msg" lines
Your sandbox may restrict `ps` or signals; if a test cannot run there, say so in notes.md. The verifying check runs outside the sandbox: from clean deps, the full suite once and the spawn suite with two more seeds, each green with no erlexec "unknown msg" line (before the fix every spawn-suite run logged one). It has 60 seconds, so do not make the suite slower.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: the two fixes, one in lib/cornerman/py/json.ex and one in lib/cornerman/spawn/run.ex, formatted, compiling with no warnings, plus ./notes.md saying what you changed in each file and why, what you ran, and anything the sandbox stopped you from verifying.
tasks.verified: the float-overflow lint case and the new spawn test pass; the full suite and two more spawn-suite runs are green with no erlexec 'unknown msg' line; only lib/cornerman/py/json.ex and lib/cornerman/spawn/run.ex changed.
